name: Emorroissa
body:
Emorroissa
CR 1/2

Not venom, but fresh blood drips from this reddish snake’s fangs while it slithers towards you through the sand.

XP 200
N Tiny magical beast
Init +3; Senses low-light vision, scent, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 16, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex +2 size)
hp 7 (1d8-1)
Fort +1, Ref +6, Will +0

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., burrow 20 ft.
Melee bite +6 (1d2-3 plus attach)
Space 2-½ ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks blood drain

STATISTICS

Str 5, Dex 18, Con 8, Int 2, Wis 11, Cha 4
Base Atk +0; CMB +2; CMD 9 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Perception +8, Stealth +16; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Attach (Ex)

When an emorroissa deals bite damage to a creature, its fangs sink into the target’s flesh. An attached emorroissa is effectively grappling its prey. The emorroissa loses its Dexterity bonus to AC and has an AC of 12 but gains a +8 racial bonus to maintain its grapple on a foe once it is attached. An attached emorroissa can be struck with a weapon or grappled itself—if its prey manages to win a grapple check or Escape Artist check against it, the emorroissa is removed.

Blood Drain (Ex)

An emorroissa drains blood at the end of its turn if it is attached to a foe, inflicting 1d2 points of damage. The emorroissa heals 1 hit point or gains point (or gains 1 temporary hit point for 1 hour (maximum 10 temporary hit points), if already at full hit points) each round it drains blood. Once an emorroissa has dealt 10 points of damage, it detaches and flees away to digest the meal. If its victim dies before the emorroissa’s appetite has been sated, the emorroissa detaches and seeks a new target.

Familiar

The master of an emorroissa familiar gains a +2 bonus on CMB checks to start and maintain a grapple.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts
Organization solitary, pair, or nest (1-8)
Treasure none

The emorroissa is not an undead, but an animal that had to acquire a taste for blood in order to keep itself hydrated in a dry, hot environment. These snakes live in deep dens under the sands, emerging to attack passing prey. Emorroisse integrate their diet with little desert reptiles and rodents.
